title: From Depletion to Conduction: The Inversion Layer

segments.text: How does a MOSFET turn on?
Apply a positive gate‑to‑source voltage and the field pushes holes away, leaving a thin depletion region of negatively charged acceptor ions.
When the gate voltage exceeds the threshold, electrons are attracted to the surface, forming an inversion layer that converts the surface from p‑type to n‑type.
This narrow n‑type channel links the heavily doped n+ source and drain, allowing electrons to flow under a drain‑to‑source voltage.
Raising the gate voltage above threshold increases electron density, so the current rises.
Below threshold only a tiny subthreshold leakage flows.
The MOSFET therefore acts as a voltage‑controlled resistor, turning on when V_G > V_th and off otherwise.
So that positive gate voltage truly creates the inversion layer.
